paragraphs: As Microsoft Threat Intelligence continues to track how threat actors operationalize AI to increase the speed, efficiency, and complexity of attacks, we’ve identified North Korean threat actors expanding their use of AI with varying levels of adoption. Threat actors use AI as a force multiplier across their operations, particularly to accelerate and scale established workflows. Recent activities illustrate this AI-enabled acceleration and scaling: Jade Sleet launched campaigns through three front companies in a single week, Onyx Sleet generated dozens of tailored lures in minutes, Coral Sleet rapidly built a new capability to trojanize private source code repositories, and Diamond Sleet used AI to enhance tailored targeting workflows, including persona development and front company creation. Further, Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet…

paragraphs: Cisco Talos observed a new AI-integrated command-and-control (C2) framework in the wild called “NIK C2.” NIK C2 contains a Windows implant, using which, an actor can dump credentials, stream the victim's keystrokes to collect the targeted victim’s sensitive data, and instruct an integrated AI model to analyze the harvested data, all within the compromised session. In this framework, the actor has abused the OpenAI Chat Completions application programming interface (API), which is a HTTP endpoint that enables ChatGPT-style conversations programmatically. In addition to the features that enable theft, an actor can also deploy desktop screen-locking ransomware via the NIK C2 implant onto the victim machine, leading to a ransom demand in Bitcoin or USDT cryptocurrencies. NIK C2 reshapes adversary tradecraft…

GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated tenants running 19.4.3-internal0 or later already include these fixes and do not need to take action. These versions address CVE-2026-111943 , along with additional unrelated bug fixes. We strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions. If you use the self-hosted version of Runners or AI Gateway, you must also upgrade those components to the latest versions; guidance is included below. Security update CVE-2026-111943 - GitLab has removed trust for compromised eMudhra Intermediate CA Certificates for GitLab CE/EE For GitLab CE/EE, GitLab has removed trust for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates whose private keys have been compromised. This release removes trust for those certificates from the certificate stores GitLab ships. For background, see eMudhra’s public incident write-up . Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions before 18.11.14, 19.0 before 19.0.11, 19.1 before 19.1.10, 19.2 before 19.2.10, 19.3 before 19.3.7, 19.4 before 19.4.5, and 19.5 before 19.5.3. Action required: update Self-Hosted GitLab Runner to version 19.5.1 Upgrading GitLab does not update GitLab Runner. Runner verifies certificates on its own, so you must also update GitLab Runner to version 19.5.1 , and rebuild any CI/CD job images that include their own ca-certificates package. To update, see the Updating the Runner page . Action required: update Self-Hosted GitLab AI Gateway to versions 18.11.8, 19.0.13, 19.1.9, 19.2.5, 19.3.3, 19.4.3, 19.5.3 Upgrading GitLab does not update the GitLab AI Gateway. (CVE-2026-95101) It was discovered that nginx incorrectly handled asynchronous file I/O in certain configurations with Server Side Includes pages. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause nginx to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-97205) It was discovered that nginx incorrectly handled SSL session ticket keys when configured with a shared session cache but without explicit ticket key rotation. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 26.10. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to forge client SSL sessions and bypass client certificate verification. These builds include Brotli 1.2.1, which fixes CVE-2026-111497 , an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Brotli decompression. In PHP Windows builds, the vulnerable decoder can be reached through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled. This is disabled by default in cURL, but applications and HTTP client libraries can enable it. The -1 suffix identifies a Windows package rebuild with updated dependencies. These builds use the same PHP source releases, and the PHP runtime versions remain unchanged. The updated packages are available on the downloads page .

paragraphs: On October 21, 2026, a compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 release was published to the Python Package Index (PyPI) and distributed through official container images. The malicious package added files that Python could execute during normal interpreter initialization. An application did not need to import LiteLLM for the payload to run: starting Python in an affected environment could be enough. Microsoft analyzed two execution paths in the affected wheels: a credential collector launched through a path extension, and a Unix-oriented loader persisted through site-specific configuration. The collector targeted authentication material across developer tools, AI applications, cloud environments, browsers, and infrastructure. A separate database module attempted to read selected credential and model-configuration records from the LiteLLM proxy. Endpoint observations on Windows and macOS…

images.alt: Diagram showing compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 installing Python startup files that automatically launch a credential collector. Stolen developer, cloud, browser, SSH, environment, and LiteLLM database data is encrypted and sent to an attacker-controlled endpoint. An optional Unix path can retrieve and execute additional Python code; this activity was not confirmed.
images.caption: Figure 1: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 execution flow.

images.alt: Python code checks the PRIVCOLLECT_ACTIVE flag, then launches the credential collector in a daemon thread or synchronously.

images.alt: Python code decodes and executes an embedded Base64- and zlib-encoded payload. The recovered Linux collector configuration specifies an upload endpoint and RSA key, and enables asynchronous collection of system, browser, SSH, shell-history, and cloud-credential data.

events.description: We suggest you set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector. This setting was already listed as a mitigation in the GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp advisory for CVE-2026-109619 published on Oct 21st, 2026. If you applied it then, keep it in place and no further action is needed. The issue can only occur under an unusual combination of configuration and application code. An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start() . Session upload progress must also still be enabled. Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 with the next release.

This publication is a security bulletin; it is not evidence that your organization has experienced a breach.

events.title: PHP issues follow-up session upload advisory
events.summary: A conditional RCE path prompts additional configuration guidance.
events.description: PHP advises disabling session upload progress until its next regular bugfix release. The issue requires an unusual configuration: a php_binary or php_serialize session handler changed to php at runtime before session_start(), with upload progress enabled. A full CVE-2026-115560 advisory is planned with the next release.
events.severityBasis: The informational advisory does not assign a severity score. Applicability depends on configuration and application behavior.
impact: Potential remote code execution in applications meeting the stated conditions.
The notice does not claim universal exposure or confirmed exploitation.
recommendations: Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 as advised by PHP and verify the effective runtime configuration.
Review whether application code changes the session serialization handler before session_start().
Track the next regular PHP release and its complete advisory.

timeline.title: Follow-up advisory published
timeline.description: PHP publishes conditional exposure details and interim configuration guidance.

events.evidenceNote: Vendor-published advisory. Unknown severity means unscored here; it does not mean low risk. Exploited=false means no exploitation assertion is made by this record.

affectedSystems: PHP applications using session upload progress with a runtime change of session serialization handler. The follow-up notice does not provide a complete affected-version range.
attackVector: A conditional remote-code-execution path involving session upload progress; the notice describes an unusual application configuration.
prerequisites: The configured session.serialize_handler is php_binary or php_serialize.
Application code changes the handler to php with ini_set() before calling session_start(), while session upload progress remains enabled.
detection: Inspect effective PHP configuration and search application initialization for runtime changes to session.serialize_handler. Confirm the order relative to session_start().
mitigation: Disable session.upload_progress.enabled until the next regular bugfix release. Retain this setting if already applied for the October 21 advisory.
limitations: The complete CVE-2026-115560 advisory was still pending in this notice. Applications that never change the handler at runtime do not meet the stated conditions.

events.severityBasis: Analyst assessment: large-scale personal-data exposure and unauthorized account changes. Capcom does not publish a formal severity rating.
impact: Email and login metadata affected: 11,774,247 records worldwide.
Additional profile fields affected: 43 records; passwords changed without authorization: 196 accounts.
Credit-card data was excluded; compromise of customers' original passwords was not confirmed.
recommendations: Treat unexpected Capcom messages as potential phishing; use official support channels.
Review account notifications and follow Capcom's account-recovery instructions.
Analyst guidance: review password reuse and monitor unusual login activity.

timeline.description: Police and the Japanese privacy regulator receive reports.

timeline.title: Public disclosure
timeline.description: Customer impact figures published.

events.evidenceNote: Counts and response reflect Capcom's October 22 disclosure. Exploited refers to a vulnerability exploitation assertion, not whether this breach occurred.

affectedSystems: CAPCOM ID account information: email addresses and identifiers including account creation, last login, login count and last-login client IP.
A subset of 43 records also included birth date, gender, country/region and nickname.
detection: Check official account notices and unexpected account changes. Treat unsolicited messages invoking the incident as potential phishing; verify through Capcom’s published support channel.
mitigation: Capcom reports blocking the unauthorized access and addressing the attack method. It reset passwords on the 196 accounts changed without authorization.
limitations: The disclosure does not explain the technical entry point. Compromise of the original customer passwords was not confirmed, and credit-card information was excluded.

events.title: Railway warns customer secrets may be exposed
events.summary: Customers urged to rotate environment variables and private registry credentials.
events.description: Railway detected anomalous activity involving systems holding customer environment variables. Its initial investigation indicates that a third party may have accessed encrypted values and decrypted some. The company recommended precautionary action for all users while determining the affected accounts.
events.severityBasis: Analyst assessment: potential exposure of reusable credentials and downstream cloud access. Railway does not assign a formal severity score.
impact: Potential exposure of API keys, database credentials and private registry credentials.
Deployments were paused during the initial investigation; this record does not establish current service availability.
Possible downstream misuse depends on the privileges of exposed credentials.
recommendations: Rotate secrets stored in Railway, including API keys and private registry credentials.
Deactivate potentially exposed AWS keys; review CloudTrail, billing and unfamiliar resources.
Disable potentially exposed Google Cloud service-account keys; review audit logs and redeploy with replacement credentials.
Verify dependent workloads use the new credentials and investigate anomalous access.

timeline.title: Incident disclosed
timeline.description: Railway issues rotation guidance and pauses deployments during investigation.

timeline.title: Cloud review guidance added
timeline.description: AWS and Google Cloud investigation instructions published.

events.evidenceNote: The disclosure is confirmed; exposure scope remains qualified as 'may have' by the provider. Recommendations include defensive analyst synthesis.

affectedSystems: Systems holding Railway customer environment variables, potentially including API keys, database secrets and private registry credentials.
attackVector: Possible unauthorized access to encrypted secret values and, for some values, plaintext; the initial access mechanism is not detailed.
prerequisites: Downstream exposure depends on which credentials were stored in Railway and the permissions attached to them. The affected account set was still under investigation.
detection: In AWS CloudTrail, review the potentially exposed access-key ID across Regions; compare unexpected resource creation, IAM changes and billing with normal operations.

In Google Cloud Audit Logs, review the service-account principal, IAM changes and unfamiliar resources. Check billing and impersonation activity; unfamiliar shared egress IPs alone do not prove misuse.
mitigation: Revoke or disable potentially exposed cloud credentials, replace the stored values and redeploy dependent workloads. Confirm the replacement credentials work and review other systems that used the old keys.
limitations: The provider describes possible exposure, not confirmed compromise of every customer. Feed status does not establish present Railway service availability.

events.title: Node.js fixes 10 flaws across supported releases
events.summary: Four High-severity fixes include a Brotli decoder RCE issue.
events.description: Node.js released security updates for the 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines. The ten listed issues include DNS handling, certificate hostname validation, Brotli memory corruption and lower-severity permission and cryptographic concerns.
events.severityBasis: Vendor-rated: the highest severity in the October 21 Node.js release is High; individual issue severities vary.
impact: Brotli decoder memory corruption can permit remote code execution in affected applications.
DNS and certificate-validation weaknesses affect security decisions; applicability varies by API usage.
recommendations: Upgrade affected supported lines to Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, or a later security-fixed release.
Rebuild and redeploy container images and bundled runtimes; verify the running version.
Review each linked advisory for application-specific exposure; migrate unsupported runtimes.

timeline.title: Security releases available
timeline.description: Fixes published for all three supported release lines.

events.evidenceNote: Patch availability does not establish deployment in your environment. CVE list here highlights the four High issues; the source covers all ten. No exploitation claim is made.

affectedSystems: Security updates are available for Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x. Exact applicability differs between the individual vulnerabilities.
The fullwidth-IP TLS verification issue affects 24.x and 26.x; the highlighted Brotli and DNS issues also affect 22.x.
attackVector: Malformed Brotli input processed by node:zlib can corrupt memory. Other fixes address mismatches between DNS resolution, input validation and TLS certificate checks.
prerequisites: Brotli exposure requires the application to decompress attacker-controlled input. DNS and TLS exposure depends on the affected APIs and hostname handling.
detection: Inventory deployed Node.js versions, including containers and bundled runtimes. Review untrusted decompression paths and investigate unusual process crashes without treating a crash alone as proof of exploitation.
mitigation: Use the security releases 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 for the corresponding branch, or a subsequent fixed release.
limitations: This record highlights four High-severity CVEs; the source describes ten issues. The release notice does not establish exploitation or patch deployment in your environment.

events.description: There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython. tarfile.tar_filter could be bypassed using crafted link entries, including symlinks with empty or directory-like names, to redirect later archive members outside the intended extraction directory. This allowed a malicious tar archive to cause tarfile.extractall() with filter="tar" to write files outside the destination directory, subject to the permissions of the extracting process. This is the tarfile.tar_filter counterpart of CVE-2026-7774, which covered tarfile.data_filter. paragraphs: Cisco Talos is aware of eight compromised intermediate certificates belonging to the intermediate certificate authority, eMudhra. Rather than possessing the mandatory 384 bits of pseudo-random security, several private keys evaluated single-digit and double-digit integers. This misconfiguration allows an attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs to impersonate any website or service. Six of the TLS certificates, trusted by Chrome, Mozilla, and Apple have been blocked by these vendors already. Two other certificates, used for codesigning by Microsoft, have also been blocked. Talos expects there will be additional patches available across a variety of technologies as software applications work to remediate the certificates’ exposure. Following the disclosure, eMudhra has revoked the compromised certificates and stopped issuing…

events.description: On 21 October 2026, the PHP project released emergency security updates (PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35) to address two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Both issues are rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 and can permit unauthenticated remote code execution on PHP installations that serve web requests. Incident Overview The vulnerabilities affect the PHP runtime itself rather than a specific application, CMS, or framework. An attacker does not necessarily need a vulnerable WordPress plugin, Laravel route, or custom application sink. The conditions can be reached during PHP’s request initialization, error handling, or cleanup phases—before application-level authentication or validation logic executes. PHP identifies the highest risk with Apache mod_php, where a demonstrated exploit can be triggered by an unauthenticated request before any application code runs. PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed deployments are also in scope. CVE-2026-109618 — RCE via out-of-memory (OOM) corruption. Out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Subsequent cleanup may treat the incomplete state as valid, enabling memory corruption that can lead to code execution. CVE-2026-109619 — RCE via stale global state / use-after-free. Request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same long-lived worker may then use the stale reference. There is no complete configuration-only mitigation. Updating the PHP runtime (or installing a trusted vendor/LTS backport) and restarting all relevant workers is the authoritative remediation. Temporary controls (disabling session.upload_progress administratively, setting memory_limit=-1 in a non-overridable context, restricting multipart POST traffic where file uploads are not required, WAF/request-size limits, etc.) can reduce specific attack paths but do not replace patching. PHP 8.1 and older are end-of-life and will not receive official upstream fixes. Organizations running those versions must obtain vendor backports or migrate to a supported branch. Bangladesh National Security Relevance PHP is widely embedded in government portals, financial services, telecommunications and ICT platforms, health systems, transportation and logistics interfaces, utilities, media, education, and vendor appliances. paragraphs: Legitimate infrastructure has become a powerful delivery mechanism for attackers, carrying the inherent trust they once had to build. As Cisco Talos explored in our previous research on weaponizing software-as-a-service (SaaS) notification pipelines, these platforms are increasingly repurposed as proxies for malicious intent. Talos has since tracked a significant acceleration in this trend, observing abuse across more than 25 distinct legitimate platforms in the past year. The abused infrastructure included collaboration, productivity, file-sharing, survey, payment, and AI-related platforms. This demonstrates that attackers are not limiting themselves to traditional phishing infrastructure or lookalike domains. Instead, they are systematically subverting the very tools businesses trust. Order notification abuse Talos recently analyzed two order notification campaigns abusing Staples and Dell transactional email pipelines.…

events.description: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately. Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs. The vulnerabilities: RCE via OOM corruption , CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w ): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. RCE via stale global state , CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. How to update: Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Source downloads are on our downloads page . Windows source and binaries are on the same page . Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance, so check your vendor for updated packages. PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version. Given the severity of these vulnerabilities, the PHP security team provided minimal source-backports for PHP 7.4 , PHP 8.0 , and PHP 8.1 to help people building from source or without access to an LTS vendor. If you cannot update immediately: while only an update is a complete solution, the following measures reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe. RCE via OOM corruption (CVE-2026-109618): Set memory_limit=-1 , preferably in a way applications can't override, such as php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration, and check that no pool, directory or application setting puts a finite limit back. This removes the controllable PHP memory limit failure, but an underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable path. Set a low post_max_size . For applications that don't require file uploads, set post_max_size = 8M . If file uploads are necessary, set post_max_size = 32M . Keep…

paragraphs: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately. Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs. The vulnerabilities: RCE via OOM corruption , CVE-2026-109618 ( GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w ): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. paragraphs: On October 21, 2026, we released versions 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10, 18.11.13 for GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE).

These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately. GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated tenants running 19.3.5-internal0 and 19.4.2-internal0 or later already include these fixes and do not need to take action.

GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases: scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays. For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ. You can see all of GitLab release blog posts here.
For security fixes, the issues detailing each vulnerability are made public on our issue tracker 90 days after the release in which they were patched.

We are committed to ensuring that all aspects of GitLab that are exposed to customers or that host customer data are held to the highest security standards. To maintain good security hygiene, it is highly recommended that all customers upgrade to the latest patch release for their supported version. You can read more best practices in securing your GitLab instance in our blog post.
Recommended Action
We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible.
When no specific deployment type (omnibus, source code, helm chart, etc.) of a product is mentioned, it means all types are affected.

CVE-2026-110264 - Integer Overflow issue in Regular Expression Compiler impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to integer overflow when compiling a specially crafted regular expression.
In addition to our standard patch releases, we have backported this fix to GitLab CE/EE versions 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, and 19.2.9.

Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 7.0 before 18.11.13, 19.0 before 19.0.10, 19.1 before 19.1.9, 19.2 before 19.2.9, 19.3 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 10.0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Thanks joaxcar for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program
Detecting CVE-2026-110264 Exploitation Attempts

GitLab security has released two threat detections to support customers with self-managed instances, listed below. GitLab-managed infrastructure, including GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, remains patched.
Onigmo native worker crash
Org mode render error burst
CVE-2026-15723 - Improper Authentication issue in OmniAuth-to-LDAP auto-linking email lookup impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, when OmniAuth SAML and LDAP auto-linking were both enabled, an authenticated user could have taken over an existing LDAP-backed account without any interaction from the targeted user, due to improper input sanitization in the LDAP email lookup path used during OmniAuth identity linking.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 10.1 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 8.2 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N)
Thanks stealthy for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program
CVE-2026-112212 - Cache Poisoning issue in OAuth/OIDC discovery endpoints impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, an unauthenticated user could have poisoned a shared cache’s OAuth/OIDC discovery document to redirect certain flows to an externally controlled server, due to improper trust of user-supplied values when constructing endpoint URLs in cached discovery responses.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 18.3 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 7.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L)
This vulnerability has been discovered internally by GitLab team member Peter Arts
CVE-2026-12664 - Improper Access Control issue in GraphQL work item email address field impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with a read_api-scoped token to retrieve a project’s incoming email address and create work items, bypassing the token’s restrictions, due to insufficient scope enforcement on a GraphQL field.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 18.2 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 6.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N)
Thanks go7f0 for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program
CVE-2026-16255 - Incomplete enforcement of instance-wide SAML/LDAP membership lock allows unauthorized member additions in GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, when the instance-wide SAML or LDAP membership lock was enabled, an authenticated user could have granted or accepted project and group membership outside the identity provider’s control, due to incomplete enforcement of the membership lock on requests created before the lock was enabled.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 12.0 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 5.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N)
Thanks 3nvz for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program
CVE-2026-105777 - Internal Credential Exposure issue in internal response headers impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, an unauthenticated user could have retrieved sensitive internal server credentials due to improper filtering of internal response headers.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 17.6.5 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)
Thanks altair00 for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program
CVE-2026-13319 - Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key issue in group milestones API impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that could have allowed an authenticated user to read milestone metadata, including titles, descriptions, and full project paths, from arbitrary private projects across the instance without any project membership, due to missing authorization checks on a user-supplied project filter parameter in the group milestones API.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 15.10 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)
Thanks a0xnirudh for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program
CVE-2026-112378 - Use of Less Trusted Source issue in AI Gateway feature enablement header impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to access paid AI features without a valid subscription due to insufficient server-side validation in billing eligibility checks.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 17.8 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N)
This vulnerability has been discovered internally by GitLab team member Halil Coban
CVE-2026-105711 - Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information issue in merge request title rendering impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, when a merge request in a public project referenced a confidential issue from a private project, an authenticated user with no project membership could have read the confidential issue’s title, due to a viewer-independent fragment cache key that incorrectly shared per-user-redacted rendered content across all users.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 15.0 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 3.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)
Thanks 20kilograma for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program
CVE-2026-14288 - Improper Access Control issue in merge request approval policy enforcement impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to bypass a required merge request approval policy on a protected branch due to improper access control during approval rule synchronization.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 17.4 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N)
CVE-2026-112326 - Improper Cleanup on Thrown Exception issue in security findings impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with read-only permissions to permanently delete existing vulnerability records due to improper cleanup logic that failed to distinguish between pre-existing records from newly created ones during error handling.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 17.8 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N)
This vulnerability has been discovered internally by GitLab team member Gregory Havenga
CVE-2026-103515 - Improper Access Control issue in group Duo admin-lock enforcement for Amazon Q settings impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, when an instance administrator locked a group’s Duo availability, an authenticated user with group Owner permissions could have re-enabled AI-backed data egress to a third-party service for that group and its descendant projects, due to insufficient granularity of the admin-lock enforcement controls.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 19.2 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1 CVSS 2.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N)

paragraphs: Frontier AI models (like Mythos) are rapidly mining decades of technical debt across ubiquitous legacy libraries, driving monthly Microsoft Patch Tuesday vulnerability advisories up more than tenfold (reaching 1,415 this month). This volume is overwhelming open-source maintainers and putting pressure on the traditional 90-day coordinated disclosure model. Despite a 105% year-over-year surge in CVEs, Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEVs) grew by only 37%, and only 3 of September's 975 Microsoft advisories saw in-the-wild exploitation, demonstrating that the vast majority of AI-discovered bugs are not practically exploited. We may be able to take new-bug-class vulnerability spikes as evidence that these vulnerabilities will eventually level off and decline, once the historical code backlog is remediated and AI verification is embedded directly into new…

paragraphs: Agents are rapidly becoming part of how work gets done. They can support a range of activities from writing code and researching products to analyzing revenue, processing expenses, and acting across the systems that run the business. To be most useful, they often need access to company data, applications, tools, and other agents. That access is what makes agents more capable. With that capability can come insider risk. This does not mean agents are inherently malicious. It means they are capable tools that can be granted access to important systems by users. They can make mistakes, be manipulated, or be compromised. Their models can produce variable outputs, their context can change, and their plans can evolve as they work. An…

This vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system. The Cisco PSIRT is aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability. CERT-EU strongly recommends updating the Content Scanner Tools package or upgrading Cisco AsyncOS Software to a fixed release as soon as possible, prioritising appliances reachable from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking all affected appliances for indicators of compromise.

paragraphs: This research was conducted jointly with Julian-Ferdinand Vögele of Recorded Future’s Insikt Group. Details of the joint research and presentation are available here. Cisco Talos identified UAT-6275 (TAG-193 by Recorded Future) activity targeting government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). Recovered artifacts show additional interest in water resources and energy. This focus is consistent with intelligence collection and may reflect the regional effects of the Russia–Ukraine war. In activity observed from June 2025 through August 2026, Talos identified four infection-chain types that use macro-enabled documents, PS2EXE downloaders, GitHub-hosted PowerShell, and a crafted WinRAR archive exploiting CVE-2025-8088. The recovered payloads include several custom reverse shells that provide interactive remote access. Three publicly accessible staging directories and GitHub repository history…

paragraphs: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8
On October 12, 2026, we released versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8 for GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE).
19.3.4 had a bug that affected merge request pages when the Ona integration was enabled. This is fixed in 19.3.5.

These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately. GitLab.com is already running the patched version. All GitLab Dedicated tenants were patched using an internal release before this patch release was published.

GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases: scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays. For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ. You can see all of GitLab release blog posts here.
For security fixes, the issues detailing each vulnerability are made public on our issue tracker 90 days after the release in which they were patched.

We are committed to ensuring that all aspects of GitLab that are exposed to customers or that host customer data are held to the highest security standards. To maintain good security hygiene, it is highly recommended that all customers upgrade to the latest patch release for their supported version. You can read more best practices in securing your GitLab instance in our blog post.
Recommended Action
We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible.
When no specific deployment type (omnibus, source code, helm chart, etc.) of a product is mentioned, it means all types are affected.

CVE-2026-97229 - Integer Overflow issue in CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 10.0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Thanks joaxcar for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
Detecting CVE-2026-97229 Exploitation Attempts

GitLab security has released six threat detections to support customers with self-managed instances, listed below. GitLab-managed infrastructure, including GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, remains patched.
Onigmo native worker crash
Graphql cilint hostile regexp
ci regexp oversized non ascii path

CVE-2026-92883 - Cross-site Scripting issue in syntax highlighting impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of other users’ browser sessions via a specially crafted repository, due to improper sanitization of HTML attributes in syntax-highlighted output.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 19.1 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 8.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N)
Thanks a0xnirudh for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.

Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 18.7 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 8.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:H/A:N)
Thanks sim4n6 for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-14814 - Permissive Regular Expression issue in repository file access impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed a user to poison cached responses for raw repository files, causing targeted users’ CI/CD pipelines to execute specially crafted content and potentially exposing protected environment variables, due to improper validation of repository references.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 8.2 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N)
Thanks ahacker1 for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-81839 - Incorrect Authorization issue in scheduled pipeline execution policy impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary CI/CD pipelines in a transferred project with the new group’s privileges due to improper cleanup of scheduled pipeline execution policy records.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 18.1 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 7.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N)
Thanks no_01 for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-96893 - Improper Neutralization of Input Used for LLM Prompting issue in GitLab Duo Agent Platform impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user to inject specially crafted content into AI agent instructions, potentially causing unintended command execution attributed to other users, due to improper neutralization of special elements in AI conversation context construction.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 19.1 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 7.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N)

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with access to GitLab Pages log data to obtain access tokens and other secrets, due to insertion of sensitive request data into log files and error tracking events.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 12.0 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 6.2 (CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N)

Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 13.11 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 5.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N)

Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 17.11 before 19.2.8, all 19.3 versions, and 19.4 before 19.4.2 CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

paragraphs: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) planning often focuses on protecting encrypted data, but authentication systems must also evolve. Certificates, trust anchors, PKI services, applications, devices, and hardware security modules may all be affected by new algorithms and larger certificate chains. Microsoft’s Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Transport Layer Security (TLS) Pilot Program helps eligible certificate authorities evaluate interoperability and operational readiness in controlled environments. Organizations should begin now by inventorying certificate dependencies, assessing vendor roadmaps, identifying long-lived infrastructure, and creating non-production test environments. Early testing can surface compatibility and process gaps before post-quantum authentication is required at scale. paragraphs: Cisco Talos identified an advanced persistent threat (APT) spear-phishing campaign against individuals affiliated with Taiwan research organizations. The operation leveraged legitimate public event themes and impersonated reputable academic and policy institutions to establish credibility. The phishing emails exhibited highly consistent structure, rhetoric, and personalization patterns, suggesting the threat actor likely used AI-assisted content generation to rapidly customize invitation lures for different targets while maintaining a common social engineering framework. Beyond traditional email phishing, the actor incorporated QR code phishing (quishing) techniques by modifying legitimate event posters with malicious QR codes, expanding the attack surface beyond email recipients to secondary victims who may encounter printed materials. The campaign deployed an advanced adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing framework that impersonated Google authentication pages and…

paragraphs: The mission of Microsoft Security’s Frontier Offensive Research & Generative Exploitation (FORGE) Lab is to advance the frontier of autonomous security engineering. events.description: We have released versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2, and 19.4.1 of the GitLab AI Gateway. These versions contain a critical security fix for GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway, and we strongly recommend that all GitLab Self-Managed customers with GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway installations update to one of these versions immediately. We have conducted targeted outreach to Self-Hosted AI Gateway customers prior to this release post with this guidance. A fix has already been deployed for GitLab-hosted AI Gateways. Customers using GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab Self-Managed instances using a GitLab-hosted AI Gateway are protected and do not need to take action. Recommended Action We strongly recommend that all GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway installations running a version affected by the issue described below are upgraded to one of the patched versions listed above as soon as possible. Security fixes Table of security fixes Title Severity Improper Neutralization issue in custom flow prompt template impacts AI Gateway Critical CVE-2026-90970 - Improper Neutralization issue in custom flow prompt template impacts AI Gateway GitLab has remediated an issue in the GitLab AI Gateway that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with Duo Agent Platform access to escape the prompt template sandbox via a specially crafted flow configuration, leading to arbitrary command execution on the AI Gateway. Impacted Versions: GitLab AI Gateway: all versions from 18.1.6 before 19.2.4, 19.3 before 19.3.2, and 19.4 before 19.4.1 CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H ) Thanks invisiblemeerkat for responsibly disclosing this issue. Updating To update GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway, see the GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway install documentation . paragraphs: We have released versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2, and 19.4.1 of the GitLab AI Gateway.

These versions contain a critical security fix for GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway, and we strongly recommend that all GitLab Self-Managed customers with GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway installations update to one of these versions immediately. We have conducted targeted outreach to Self-Hosted AI Gateway customers prior to this release post with this guidance.

A fix has already been deployed for GitLab-hosted AI Gateways. Customers using GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab Self-Managed instances using a GitLab-hosted AI Gateway are protected and do not need to take action.
Recommended Action

We strongly recommend that all GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway installations running a version affected by the issue described below are upgraded to one of the patched versions listed above as soon as possible.
Security fixes
Table of security fixes
Improper Neutralization issue in custom flow prompt template impacts AI Gateway
Critical
CVE-2026-90970 - Improper Neutralization issue in custom flow prompt template impacts AI Gateway

GitLab has remediated an issue in the GitLab AI Gateway that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with Duo Agent Platform access to escape the prompt template sandbox via a specially crafted flow configuration, leading to arbitrary command execution on the AI Gateway.
Impacted Versions: GitLab AI Gateway: all versions from 18.1.6 before 19.2.4, 19.3 before 19.3.2, and 19.4 before 19.4.1 CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Thanks invisiblemeerkat for responsibly disclosing this issue.
Updating
To update GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway, see the GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway install documentation.
Receive Patch Notifications
To receive release notifications via RSS, subscribe to our patch release RSS feed or our RSS feed for all releases.

events.title: [Security-announce][CVE-2026-19445] Use-after-free of a server-side SSLContext when sni_callback switches contexts
events.summary: There is a CRITICAL severity vulnerability affecting CPython. A remote, unauthenticated TLS client can make a server crash or call through a freed pointer if its sni_callback assigns a different context to SSLSocket.context (the documented way to select a certificate per server name) and nothing else keeps the original ssl.SSLContext alive.…
events.description: There is a CRITICAL severity vulnerability affecting CPython. A remote, unauthenticated TLS client can make a server crash or call through a freed pointer if its sni_callback assigns a different context to SSLSocket.context (the documented way to select a certificate per server name) and nothing else keeps the original ssl.SSLContext alive. Typical cases are servers that create an SSLContext per connection or replace it while connections are open; servers that wrap their listening socket with it are not affected. Mitigation: keep a reference to every SSLContext that sets sni_callback for the lifetime of the server. TLS clients are not affected. Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions: * https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19445 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/158504

events.summary: There is a HIGH severity vulnerability affecting CPython. `ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio()` didn't require the `server_hostname` argument to not be `None` if `ssl.SSLContext.check_hostname` was set. Due to a missing parameter check in `SSLObject`, if the `server_hostname` argument isn't supplied then hostname verification would be silently skipped.…
events.description: There is a HIGH severity vulnerability affecting CPython. `ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio()` didn't require the `server_hostname` argument to not be `None` if `ssl.SSLContext.check_hostname` was set. Due to a missing parameter check in `SSLObject`, if the `server_hostname` argument isn't supplied then hostname verification would be silently skipped. This defect could lead to programs where certificate hostname verification *appeared* to be succeeding with `SSLContext.check_hostname = True` and no `ValueError` being raised due to misconfiguration. If the program passes a `server_hostname` value that isn't an empty string or `None` to any of these APIs then certificate hostname verification proceeds as expected and the program is not affected by this vulnerability. Mitigating this vulnerability doesn't require updating Python or applying the patch. To mitigate, pass a valid non-`None` and non-empty `server_hostname` value to `SSLContext.wrap_bio()`, `asyncio.create_connection()`, or `asyncio.loop.start_tls()` and certificate hostname verification will proceed as expected. Upgrading to the latest version of Python or applying the patch only changes the behavior from silently skipping hostname verification to raising a `ValueError`, similar to `SSLContext.wrap_socket()`, when `server_hostname` isn't supplied. Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions: * https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19553 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/158503

events.description: There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython. The cleanup of tempfile.TemporaryDirectory is vulnerable to a race condition. An attacker who can modify the tree during cleanup can replace a directory with a symbolic link, causing files outside of the temporary directory to be deleted or have their permissions and file flags reset, with the privileges of the process performing the cleanup. Note that platforms where shutil.rmtree.avoids_symlink_attacks is false, remain affected, and file flags may still be reset outside of the tree on all platforms. Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions: * https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12345 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157580

paragraphs: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.4.1, 19.3.3, 19.2.7
On September 23, 2026, we released versions 19.4.1, 19.3.3, 19.2.7 for GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE).

These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately. GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action.

GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases: scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays. For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ. You can see all of GitLab release blog posts here.
For security fixes, the issues detailing each vulnerability are made public on our issue tracker 90 days after the release in which they were patched.

We are committed to ensuring that all aspects of GitLab that are exposed to customers or that host customer data are held to the highest security standards. To maintain good security hygiene, it is highly recommended that all customers upgrade to the latest patch release for their supported version. You can read more best practices in securing your GitLab instance in our blog post.
Recommended Action
We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible.
When no specific deployment type (omnibus, source code, helm chart, etc.) of a product is mentioned, it means all types are affected.

CVE-2026-89078 - Double Free issue in Regular Expression Parser impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to a double free issue when parsing a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 19.2 before 19.2.7, 19.3 before 19.3.3, and 19.4 before 19.4.1 CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:L)
Thanks joaxcar for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program
CVE-2026-93577 - Integer Overflow issue in Regular Expression Compiler impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to an integer overflow issue when compiling a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 19.2 before 19.2.7, 19.3 before 19.3.3, and 19.4 before 19.4.1 CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)

paragraphs: On September 23, 2026, we released versions 19.0.9 and 18.11.12 for GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE).

These versions backport the fixes for two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-85706 and CVE-2026-87719, that were originally patched in 19.3.2, 19.2.6, and 19.1.8 on September 10, 2026. These backports were made available outside of our standard maintenance policy so that self-managed administrators running 18.11 and 19.0 can apply the fixes without first completing a version upgrade. These versions contain no other changes.

We strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations still running 18.11 or 19.0 be upgraded to one of these versions immediately. Installations running 19.1, 19.2, or 19.3 should upgrade to 19.1.8, 19.2.6, or 19.3.2 or later instead. GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action.

GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases: scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays. For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ. You can see all GitLab release blog posts.
For security fixes, the issues detailing each vulnerability are made public on our issue tracker 90 days after the release in which they were patched.

We are committed to ensuring that all aspects of GitLab that are exposed to customers or that host customer data are held to the highest security standards. To maintain good security hygiene, it is highly recommended that all customers upgrade to the latest patch release for their supported version. You can read more best practices in securing your GitLab instance in our blog post.
Recommended Action
We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible.
When no specific deployment type (omnibus, source code, Helm chart, etc.) of a product is mentioned, it means all types are affected.
Security fixes
The fixes in these versions are the same fixes that were released in 19.1.8, 19.2.6, and 19.3.2 on September 10, 2026.
Table of security fixes
Path Traversal issue in repository commits API impacts GitLab CE/EE
Critical
Insecure Deserialization issue in GraphQL subscription serializer impacts GitLab EE
CVE-2026-85706 - Path Traversal issue in repository commits API impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, an unauthenticated user could have read arbitrary files from the GitLab server due to improper path confinement and missing authentication enforcement in the repository commits API.

Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 18.7 before 18.11.12, 19.0 before 19.0.9, 19.1 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 10.0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N)
Thanks s3ntago for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
Detecting CVE-2026-85706 Exploitation Attempts

CVE-2026-85706 has been added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. GitLab-managed infrastructure, including GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, remains patched. GitLab security has released three threat detections to support customers with self-managed instances:
GitLab LFI attempt reading gitlab.yml
GitLab LFI via metadata.path parameter
GitLab LFI file path attempt
CVE-2026-87719 - Insecure Deserialization issue in GraphQL subscription serializer impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could allow an authenticated user with Duo Chat access to obtain Advanced Search instance configurations and sensitive credentials using a specially crafted GraphQL subscription argument to bypass serialization and perform server object lookup.

Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 18.3 before 18.11.12, 19.0 before 19.0.9, 19.1 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Thanks kyyblin for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
Bug fixes
These versions contain the security fixes listed above only. They do not contain any other bug fixes.
Important notes on upgrading

19.0.9 and 18.11.12 are backport releases for self-managed installations that cannot immediately move to a supported 19.1 or later version. Upgrading to the latest supported version remains the recommended path, because 18.11 and 19.0 do not receive the other fixes included in 19.1.8, 19.2.6, and 19.3.2.
To learn more about the impact of upgrades on your installation, see:
Zero-downtime upgrades for multi-node deployments
Standard upgrades for single-node installations
Updating
To update GitLab, see the Update page. To update GitLab Runner, see the Updating the Runner page.
Receive Patch Notifications

To receive patch blog notifications delivered to your inbox, visit our contact us page. To receive release notifications via RSS, subscribe to our patch release RSS feed or our RSS feed for all releases.

events.description: There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython. When tarfile extracts a link on a system that doesn't support links, it falls back to extracting a member from the archive. In this case, the filter function is run twice: once for the extracted member, and once with name set to the location of the link. For one of the calls, the return value was ignored. Instead, the member should be skipped if either call returns None. Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions: * https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-87910 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157266

paragraphs: On 9 September 2026, Check Point released emergency security updates addressing two critical vulnerabilities affecting Check Point Security Gateway, Security Management Server, and Spark Firewall deployments configured to use Remote Access VPN or Site-to-Site VPN. Both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS score of 9.8 and could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on affected appliances. CERT-EU strongly recommends applying the available hotfixes as soon as possible, prioritising internet-facing and perimeter appliances.

paragraphs: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.3.2, 19.2.6, 19.1.8

Update: On September 23, 2026, we backported fixes for CVE-2026-85706 and CVE-2026-87719 to versions 19.0.9 and 18.11.12 of GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE). Self-managed GitLab administrators running older versions of GitLab CE and EE can now upgrade to these versions to apply these security fixes.
On September 10, 2026, we released versions 19.3.2, 19.2.6, 19.1.8 for GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE).

These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately. GitLab.com is already running the patched version. GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action.

GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases: scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays. For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ. You can see all of GitLab release blog posts here.
For security fixes, the issues detailing each vulnerability are made public on our issue tracker 90 days after the release in which they were patched.

We are committed to ensuring that all aspects of GitLab that are exposed to customers or that host customer data are held to the highest security standards. To maintain good security hygiene, it is highly recommended that all customers upgrade to the latest patch release for their supported version. You can read more best practices in securing your GitLab instance in our blog post.
Recommended Action
We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible.
When no specific deployment type (omnibus, source code, helm chart, etc.) of a product is mentioned, it means all types are affected.

CVE-2026-85706 - Path Traversal issue in repository commits API impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, an unauthenticated user could have read arbitrary files from the GitLab server due to improper path confinement and missing authentication enforcement in the repository commits API.

Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 18.7 before 18.11.12, 19.0 before 19.0.9, 19.1 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 10.0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N)
Thanks s3ntago for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
Detecting CVE-2026-85706 Exploitation Attempts

CVE-2026-85706 has been added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. GitLab-managed infrastructure, including GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, remains patched. GitLab security has released three threat detections to support customers with self-managed instances:
GitLab LFI attempt reading gitlab.yml
GitLab LFI via metadata.path parameter
GitLab LFI file path attempt
CVE-2026-87719 - Insecure Deserialization issue in GraphQL subscription serializer impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could allow an authenticated user with Duo Chat access to obtain Advanced Search instance configurations and sensitive credentials using a specially crafted GraphQL subscription argument to bypass serialization and perform server object lookup.

Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 18.3 before 18.11.12, 19.0 before 19.0.9, 19.1 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Thanks kyyblin for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-88765 - Buffer Overflow issue in Unicode conversion wrapper impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could allow an authenticated user to achieve remote code execution by importing a specially crafted Git project export to overflow the Unicode conversion buffer used in Advanced Search indexing.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 12.3 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 8.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Thanks joaxcar for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-79708 - Scheduled Pipeline Execution Policy test allows Developers to access protected CI/CD variables

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with developer permissions to execute a policy test pipeline on projects within their group and access protected CI/CD variables restricted to higher-privileged roles due to insufficient scope validation.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 19.0 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 8.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:H/A:N)
Thanks yvvdwf for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-78252 - Cross-site Scripting issue in Markdown JSON table renderer impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, an authenticated user could have induced a targeted user to perform unintended state-changing HTTP requests due to improper sanitization of user-controlled data in the Markdown JSON table renderer.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 15.3 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 8.2 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:L)
Thanks a_m_a_m for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-13210 - Incorrect Authorization issue in CI/CD environment variable scope matcher impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user to access CI/CD variables outside their intended environment scope due to improper input validation in the environment scope pattern matcher.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 15.7 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 7.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N)
Thanks nwicks for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2025-14871 - Denial of Service issue in GraphQL complexity limiter impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to cause denial of service due to improper resource allocation limits in the GraphQL complexity calculation logic.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 18.4.6 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 7.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H)
Thanks hunter0xp7 for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-1168 - Denial of Service issue in GraphQL complexity limiter impacts GitLab CE/EE
CVE-2024-11222 - Race Condition issue in Merge Request Pipelines impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed a developer user to perform actions in the context of another user’s merge request commit due to a race condition issue in pipeline creation.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 13.0 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 6.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N)
Thanks xorz for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-12910 - Improper Authentication issue in SAML SSO sign-in restriction enforcement impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user to bypass SAML SSO sign-in restrictions and authenticate without SSO due to missing authentication enforcement checks.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 18.6 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 5.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N)
Thanks theluci for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-82837 - Insufficiently Protected Credentials issue in Workhorse senddata emitters impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user to access sensitive credentials and tokens without transiting the expected proxy due to improper authorization checks on internal data emission endpoints.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 10.1.0 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)
Thanks 0xoroot for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-19619 - Cross-site Scripting issue in Content Editor impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of a targeted user’s session due to improper sanitization of pasted HTML content in the Content Editor.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 19.0 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 4.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N)
Thanks lucvs for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-86341 - Access Control Implementation issue in protected environment approval rules impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, an authenticated user with Owner or Maintainer permissions could have silently disabled protected environment deployment approval requirements, allowing unapproved deployments to reach production due to improper access control checks performed after the protected resource was modified.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 17.1 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 4.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N)
This vulnerability has been discovered internally by GitLab team member Peter Arts.
CVE-2026-86340 - Authorization Bypass issue in protected environment approval rules impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could allow an authenticated user to bypass required deployment approvals for protected environments by deleting the sole approver group or user account.
CVE-2026-7514 - Missing Authorization issue in Generic Package Registry impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that an authenticated user with developer-role permissions could substitute package file content and hide packages from their owners due to improper authorization checks in the Generic Package Registry.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 13.9 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N)
Thanks toofikz for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-8030 - Improper Input Validation issue in Namespace Transfer impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user to prevent another user from modifying their group settings due to improper validation of group URL slugs during namespace transfers.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 13.0 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L)
Thanks mateuszek for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-16794 - Missing Authorization issue in Compliance Framework management impacts GitLab EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with the Security Manager role to execute arbitrary CI/CD jobs and access protected variables within group projects due to improper authorization controls on compliance framework management.
Impacted Versions: GitLab EE: all versions from 18.11 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N)
Thanks manual_mint for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.
CVE-2026-3855 - Improper Input Validation issue in Terraform State API impacts GitLab CE/EE

GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with project-level permissions to access restricted file contents on the server or cause denial of service due to improper validation of parameters in the Terraform state upload functionality.
Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 18.2.7 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2 CVSS 3.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)
Thanks ahacker1 for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program.

events.description: On 8 September 2026, as part of its September Security Patch Day, SAP released Security Notes addressing two critical vulnerabilities affecting a broad range of SAP products[3]. The most severe, CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), is a memory corruption vulnerability in SAP Extended Passport (EPP) processing, nicknamed "OVERPASS" by the Onapsis Research Labs (ORL), which discovered and responsibly disclosed it[3]. The second, CVE-2026-58240 (CVSS 9.8), nicknamed "S4GET", is a missing authentication check in the SAP NetWeaver Message Server[6]. Both are remotely exploitable without authentication. According to the reporting researchers, successful exploitation of either can result in arbitrary operating system command execution under the account that owns the SAP installation, leading to full compromise of the affected system and the business data it holds[6]. CERT-EU strongly recommends applying SAP Security Notes 3747649 and 3759472 as soon as possible.

events.summary: There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython. events.description: There is a MEDIUM severity vulnerability affecting CPython. The tarfile module's tar and data extraction filters created directories outside the destination for members whose name leaves the destination and returns to it, such as ../evil/../dest/sub/file. The containment check used the resolved path, but intermediate directories were created from the name as given. Only empty directories are created outside the destination. Member contents are still extracted inside it. To return to the destination the member's name must contain the destination directory's own final component, so extraction into a secure randomised directory is not affected. This affects POSIX platforms only. On Windows, .. components are collapsed before the path reaches the filesystem, so the directories outside the destination are never created. Please see the linked CVE ID for the latest information on affected versions: * https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19672 * https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/156000
